newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro power industry faces shortages - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro power industry faces shortages - Tanjug.

text.p: Montenegro power industry Elektroprivreda Crne Gore cannot produce enough power to meet the republic's needs and has no money for imports, state news agency Tanjug reported Tuesday.

Out of Montenegro's daily consumption of over 10 million KWh of electricity it secures only 3.4 million KWh from its own sources, a statement issued by Elektroprivreda Crne Gore was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
"Instead of repaying its due electricity debts of 2.4 million KWh a day to Romania and Macedonia, Montenegro is forced to get even more indebted," the power company's statement said.

Montenegro's hydroelectric power plant Perucica produces only 900,000 KWh a day, or some 15 percent of its capacity. It has had to adapt production to its accumulated water reserves of 40 million KWh, of which it can only use 25 million KWh in respect of the required water minimum.
The remaining 2.5 million KWh accounting for Montenegro's production are provided through cooperation deals with Serbia, Yugoslavia's second federal unit.
Montenegro has to import the rest. The republic daily purchases 3.6 million KWh from the Bosnian Serb Republic, 2.4 million from Romania and 1.2 million from Albania.

Elektroprivreda Crne Gore urged consumers, especially big ones, to reduce to maximum electricity consumption because it cannot meet costs of large electricity imports due to high outstanding claims from consumers and unpaid debts to its suppliers, the statement said.

Tanjug last week reported the power company asked the Montenegrin government for a $1.8 million loan which it planned to repay by July and for the government's help in recovering claims from big power consumers. -- Beti Bilandzic, 381 11 222 4305
